title: CritBoard — zero-token fleet mission control at :9999
description: Build and maintain CritBoard (http://10.0.0.5:9999/), a mission-control UI monitoring every bead, agent, and worktree across the fleet, plus token usage and spend. Repo: github.com/demo-org/demo-dashboard, working tree ~/work/dashboard. Hard constraint: the running dashboard makes ZERO LLM calls -- collectors are subprocess+file parsing only. Layout is data (config/layout.json) so the UI can be reshaped without code changes.
acceptance_criteria: 1. http://10.0.0.5:9999/ serves the dashboard. 2. Beads, agents, worktrees, token spend all render live. 3. No LLM API call is made by any collector. 4. Editing config/layout.json changes the panel layout with no JS edit.

title: demo-lms-content: PR #238 shipped a false 'human-reviewed' provenance claim — audit the batch
description:
PR #238 (content batch: correcting a factual error) flips review_status on two lesson interactions from 'pending  # AI-drafted, not yet human-reviewed, matches metadata.review.status' to 'approved  # human-reviewed 2026-09-04'. The flip was made by an automated account in a later commit; no human reviewed it. The PR body still describes the field as 'pending', and the lesson's own metadata.review.status is still pending, so the diff contradicts both its description and the file it edits.

VERIFIED CONVENTION on main (2026-09-18): every other 'approved' value uses '# verified: <specific fact/arithmetic checked>' -- self-attested content verification, never a human-review claim. #238 would be the first false human-review assertion in the repo.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE PR: review_status is the signal that tells anyone downstream whether curriculum content has had human eyes on it. A bot writing 'human-reviewed <date>' destroys the meaning of the field. This is also live-deploying content (merge to main goes live within 60s).

ACTION: a scan of all remaining open PRs for added/altered review_status lines is running; results at scratchpad/provenance-scan.txt. Any other PR asserting human review must be corrected the same way (revert to pending). Consider a validator rule that rejects any review_status annotation claiming human review, since no automated process can legitimately write one.
notes:
SCAN COMPLETE 2026-09-18 across all open PRs (diff-level grep for added review_status lines).

A small number of PRs add a false human-review claim, all dated the same day -- a scripted batch flip, not a judgement call. All read: review_status: approved  # human-reviewed 2026-09-04

Everything else is honest: the large majority of added review_status lines use 'unreviewed'; the rest use 'approved' (the false ones plus legitimate '# verified:' style).

ON MAIN: 0 false claims. Convention confirmed: pending markers say 'not yet human-reviewed'; approved markers say '# verified: <specific check>'. So nothing false has shipped to production YET -- all are still gated behind open PRs. #238 is already being corrected.

REMAINING WORK: apply the same revert-to-pending fix to the other flagged PRs when they reach the front of the queue, and add a validator rule rejecting any review_status annotation that claims human review.

title: demo-web PR #3: 44 unresolved review threads and round 4 never requested
description:
HANDOFF-CRITICAL. The adversarial review loop is mid-flight and must not be abandoned -- done means PASS on the current head per `review_loop.sh close`, not 'the fixes are merged'.

STATE 2026-09-15: PR #3 on demo-org/demo-web, branch phase-1/registry, head efc8d50, mergeable, reviewDecision CHANGES_REQUESTED. 44 unresolved threads. Loop state PUSHED_NOT_REQUESTED.

Review has blocked THREE rounds and found a genuine P1 every single round. Left unreviewed this PR would have shipped with: an orphaned public archive page, a proxy-200 hole that unlocks sending with nothing published, and a consumed single-use recipient snapshot with no recovery. All three are now fixed and merged. Round 4 has NOT been requested on efc8d50.

HOW TO REQUEST: write a round-4 file, validate it with review_round.sh check 4 (it enforces a real grep-enumerated site list, every claim mapped to a real test name or marked UNPROVEN, and refuses a repeat Invariant-id with the same predicate shape), then post via the request script asserting dropped == []. Hard limit 2000 chars on the posted message. Then sync state to the requested head.

DO NOT run another automated review loop beyond the one agreed pass.

Acceptance:
1. PASS/FAIL: round-4 file passes review_round.sh check 4.
2. PASS/FAIL: request posted on the exact full 40-char head with dropped == [].
3. PASS/FAIL: every finding either fixed with a named commit or dispositioned in writing -- no silent skips.
4. PASS/FAIL: review_loop.sh close exits 0 (PASS on the current head). That is the definition of done.

title: demo-web: build the inbound server -- suppression callback plus the approval preview
description:
This is the next substantial build and it unblocks two things at once.

The control-plane hostname resolves to its host but nothing serves it yet: http 301, https no response -- no vhost, no certificate.

TWO SURFACES, deliberately different in kind:
1. /callbacks/suppression -- MACHINE ONLY, signed, per docs/contracts/signed-registry-api.md. The primary system tells the control plane about new suppressions so queued unsent recipients stop. Carries a hashed identifier only, never a plain address. Fire-and-forget: a failed callback must never delay the primary suppression path, which already works today via a durable outbox.
2. /preview/<token> -- HUMAN FACING. The approval magic link, bound to the content hash so an approver reads the exact bytes that will be sent and cannot approve a later edited revision. Currently a placeholder base URL 404s. This is what turns approval from machine-driven into a human clicking a link.

EVERYTHING ELSE 404s. No homepage, no index, nothing browsable.

DESIGN CONSTRAINTS: do a mechanical rename first as one no-behaviour-change commit, before any inbound file exists, so the rename never shares a diff with a new hole. The server binds LOCALHOST only; a reverse proxy terminates TLS. Only the byte-moving mechanics live in the allowlisted file; parsing, signature verification, and every state change stay outside, testable without a socket. The offline network-isolation proof must keep passing.

A LISTENING SOCKET HAS A LARGER BLAST RADIUS THAN AN OUTBOUND CALL. This needs its own review pass: signature verified before ANY state change, request-size cap, bounded reads, refusal of every path but the two above, and no information disclosure in error responses.

The target host is a SHARED production host running other live workloads. Reload the proxy, never restart, and verify the existing sites answer before and after.

Acceptance:
1. PASS/FAIL: the rename lands as its own no-behaviour-change commit first.
2. PASS/FAIL: a correctly signed suppression callback is accepted and stops a queued recipient; an unsigned or forged one is refused before any state change, proven by a test naming the failing check.
3. PASS/FAIL: an approval preview token renders the exact revision bytes and is refused once expired or once the revision is superseded.
4. PASS/FAIL: every other path returns 404.
5. PASS/FAIL: the process is not reachable except through the proxy.
6. PASS/FAIL: offline proof still passes; check-boundaries still refuses an unlisted file and a non-allowlisted importer.
7. PASS/FAIL: existing production sites verified unaffected before and after.
8. PASS/FAIL: each test break-tested with review_round.sh breaktest, FAIL-then-PASS output pasted.

title: demo-web: LIVE STATE as of 2026-09-15 -- read this before touching the production site
description:
Orientation for whoever picks this up. The system is PARTLY LIVE on a real production website. Read this before changing anything.

WHAT IS LIVE (at the production host, under a non-root path):
- Plugin deployed and active at head efc8d50. Several feature-flag constants set in the host config.
- Public signup published, deliberately NOT linked from any menu.
- Double opt-in works end to end. A GET on a confirm link deliberately does nothing; only a nonce-carrying POST confirms.
- All signed API endpoints answer and refuse unsigned callers with 401 unknown_key_id.
- THIS WEEK'S CONTENT IS ALREADY PUBLIC -- real content, published by the cycle runner during a dry run. It has NOT been sent to anyone.
- The scheduled task driving the cron path runs every 5 min, alerting after 3 consecutive failures.
- Staff registry: a small number of active admins.
- Confirmed test subscribers exist.

WHAT IS NOT LIVE: the control plane has no runtime and is NOT deployed. The control-plane hostname resolves but nothing serves it.

TRAPS THAT COST REAL TIME HERE:
1. The homepage is served by a full-page cache, so server code does not run on it. To trigger anything server-side, hit an UNCACHED url such as the admin login path.
2. The DNS host can reuse the SOA serial on a zone edit, so nameservers never reload and a record silently never appears. Always verify the serial advanced.
3. There is NO route to a database backup: the panel's backup feature is disabled, the alternate backup API 401s, and the DB is on a SEPARATE host whose port is firewalled. The only rollback assets are config copies kept elsewhere.
4. Outbound mail from this host is SLOW (greylisting), not dropped. Confirmation emails arrive minutes late. Do not diagnose a missing email until you have waited.
5. A login-security plugin locks out an IP after repeated failed login attempts. Do not brute-force a password check.
6. The panel's cron feature is DISABLED on this account -- that is why the scheduler lives on the other host.

Acceptance: PASS/FAIL -- this bead is read and acknowledged before any change to the live site.
